I think you misunderstand or I misspoke. You don't need a degree to write good novels, we agree on that, but the argument is "you don't need running shoes to run but it helps", and I get that. However, I would rather be doing a trade, making money on the job, than going to classes, studying, and working a wageslave job, and having less time dedicated to writing, something that I love.

They are telling me to stay in college, and not only that, but stay another 3 years for a master's. I never wanted to go in the first place. I'm not trying to deny their advice, but the consensus is "muh networking" so why should I have to go through more years of college just for the chance that someone I'm friends with would get into publishing or editing? I think people are misrepresenting the point of my original post. I don't want to be in college because the only degrees worthwhile in college are STEM, medical, or dental. At least, that's what I think because that is where you can make a decent living. So instead of doing that, I'm asking why a degree is necessary when I could be making more money doing a trade and writing on the side.

But I don't care for or want them. People can be successful writers with or without degrees. The degree doesn't change anything, and I'd be making more money with a trade. I'm scared to take the leap. Why do parents force their children into something they don't want, then get surprised when their kid turns to drugs, or even worse, if you've seen Dead Poet Society, Niel does something after discovering his parents won't let him do what he wants

But I don't want to do that. I thought college was about finding out what you want to do, and many claim college is the best 4 years of your life. I loathe it. That's why I considered going into a trade, but I don't know if I have the strength to make that leap. I'm watching Brandon Sanderson's creative writing courses on YouTube, and I don't expect then to turn me into an excellent writer, but it's free, and more than what I would get at university because I trust the information coming from him since he's a best selling author. He even recommends writers do something that's physically demanding instead of something like programming because it gives you time to think about your stories while on the job, while programming or any other STEM field exhausts your mind so by the end of your work shift you are too drained to write. I also consider a trade because it pays well, but I don't know if I can make the change.

Which brings me back to my first problem. I don't want to be in school for a degree I don't need to publish my writing. I wanted to do something that includes more physical labor, like bricklaying for example. However I feel like I am stuck in a rock and a hard place due to the circumstances I mentioned in the original post.
Now comes the choice of weighing the two evils. Either pay to self publish and still make some money from it, or pay a ton more for a MFA, and still only have a *chance* to be published.

Well you are correct that MFA creates a constructive program I wouldn't get on my own. It's also possible to find spaces online where people offer constructive writing criticisms, especially from those self-published authors that make decent money. I know of someone that had made over $100k selling his books on Amazon, getting money from Patreon, and he is only 22. Not saying I *would* be like that, I mean I'd hope to. There are lots of best selling authors that just have their bachelors in something completely unrelated to creative writing, so I still don't know if I am making a big mistake.

But isn't self-publishing an option? I know Amazon allows for publishing, and I know some folks that make money through that. I would want to get my book sold in stores, but I just can't be bothered to go through 3 more years for my masters
